name: kdb+
tagline: Column-store time-series engine with the q language, a fixture of capital-markets tick data.
description: kdb+ from KX is a compact column-oriented database fused with q, a terse vector programming language, and has been the default tick-data store at banks, exchanges and hedge funds for two decades. The classic setup, a tickerplant feeding an in-memory real-time database while history is written to date-partitioned splayed files, delivers very fast queries over long time ranges on modest hardware. In November 2025 KX made KDB-X, the next generation of kdb+, generally available, together with a Community Edition that is free for personal and commercial use within resource limits, and PyKX for working from Python. The q learning curve and commercial licensing at scale remain the main barriers.

license.name: Commercial; KDB-X Community Edition free with resource limits

pricing.notes: Community Edition is free with core and memory limits; production licences and kdb Insights are negotiated with KX.

managedServices.name: Amazon FinSpace with Managed kdb Insights

scale.notes: Scale out by partitioning history across segments and hosts behind q gateways; real-time data lives in RAM.

strengths: Very low-latency analytics over in-memory and date-partitioned on-disk tables
As-of and window joins built for trade/quote alignment
Tiny binary and footprint; runs well on a single large server
Tickerplant pub/sub pattern unifies real-time and historical queries
Decades of production use in front-office finance
weaknesses: q is terse and niche; hiring and onboarding are hard
Commercial licensing at scale is expensive and opaque
Clustering, HA and replication are build-it-yourself architecture patterns
Small open-source ecosystem compared with SQL databases
useCases: Equities, FX and futures tick capture
Quant research on historical market data
High-frequency sensor data in telecoms and manufacturing
notIdealFor: Teams without q or PyKX expertise
